[latex]a={*}\text{ptr}[/latex] → [latex]a=50[/latex].
[latex]({*}\text{ptr})++[/latex] → increments [latex]\text{arr[1]}[/latex] from [latex]50[/latex] to [latex]51[/latex].
[latex]\text{ptr}++[/latex] → now points to [latex]\text{arr[2]}=10[/latex] (unaffected).

[latex]\text{printf}[/latex] computes [latex]a+({*}\text{ptr})+\text{arr[1]}=50+10+51=111[/latex] (using [latex]\text{arr[1]}[/latex]'s updated value [latex]51[/latex], since the increment already happened).

questions.text:
int x=126,y=105;
 do {
	 if(x>y) x=x-y; 
	else y=y-x; 
      } while(x!=y); 

printf("%d",x);
The output of the given C code segment is ________. (Answer in integer)
questions.solution:
This loop is exactly the subtraction-based Euclidean algorithm for computing [latex]\gcd(x,y)[/latex], repeatedly subtracting the smaller from the larger until they're equal (which happens exactly at their GCD).

[latex]\gcd(126,105)[/latex]: [latex]126-105=21[/latex]; then [latex]105-21=84[/latex]; [latex]84-21=63[/latex]; [latex]63-21=42[/latex]; [latex]42-21=21[/latex] — now [latex]x=y=21[/latex], loop ends.

Answer: 21

[latex]a="@\#Hello\ World!"[/latex] occupies indices [latex]0[/latex]-[latex]14[/latex] (`@`,`#`,`H`,`e`,`l`,`l`,`o`,` `,`W`,`o`,`r`,`l`,`d`,`!`,`\0`). [latex]\text{stringcopy(a, a+2)}[/latex] sets [latex]s=a[/latex] (index [latex]0[/latex]) and [latex]t=a+2[/latex] (index [latex]2[/latex]), copying forward while [latex]{*}t[/latex] is non-null (checked before each copy).

Since the loop condition is checked before copying, it copies indices [latex]2[/latex] through [latex]13[/latex] (`H` through `!`, [latex]12[/latex] characters) into destination indices [latex]0[/latex] through [latex]11[/latex], then stops as soon as [latex]{*}t[/latex] hits the original null at index [latex]14[/latex] — without ever writing a new null terminator into the destination.

So after the copy: indices [latex]0[/latex]-[latex]11[/latex] hold the shifted text `Hello World!`, but indices [latex]12,13,14[/latex] still hold their original, untouched values: `d`, `!`, and the original `\0`.

[latex]\text{printf("\%s")}[/latex] prints from index [latex]0[/latex] until it hits the first null — which is still the original one at index [latex]14[/latex]. So it prints: `Hello World!` (indices 0-11) followed by the leftover `d` (index 12) and `!` (index 13) before finally stopping at the null.

Answer: Hello World!d!

[latex]\text{gate(14362)}[/latex] first works out that [latex]14362[/latex] has [latex]5[/latex] digits (via the [latex]t[/latex]-scaling loop), then peels off digits from most significant to least significant, keeping every other digit starting from the 2nd digit (since [latex]turn[/latex] starts at [latex]0[/latex] — skip, then keep, skip, keep, ...).

Digits of [latex]14362[/latex] in order: [latex]1,4,3,6,2[/latex].
[latex]turn=0[/latex]: digit [latex]1[/latex] — skipped.
[latex]turn=1[/latex]: digit [latex]4[/latex] — kept, [latex]newnum=4[/latex].
[latex]turn=0[/latex]: digit [latex]3[/latex] — skipped.
[latex]turn=1[/latex]: digit [latex]6[/latex] — kept, [latex]newnum=4\times10+6=46[/latex].
[latex]turn=0[/latex]: digit [latex]2[/latex] — skipped.

Final [latex]newnum=46[/latex].

Answer: 46

questions.text:
#include <stdio.h>  
int foo(int S[],int size){  
    if(size == 0) return 0;  
    if(size == 1) return 1;  
    if(S[0] != S[1]) return 1+foo(S+1,size-1);  
    return foo(S+1,size-1);  
}  
int main(){  
    int A[]={0,1,2,2,2,0,0,1,1};  
    printf("%d",foo(A,9));  
    return 0;  
}
The value printed by the given C program is _________. (Answer in integer).
questions.solution:
Trace the recursion on [latex]A=[0,1,2,2,2,0,0,1,1][/latex] (comparing each element to its immediate neighbor, adding [latex]1[/latex] whenever they differ):

[latex] egin{array}{l}foo([0,1,\ldots])=1+foo([1,2,\ldots])\quad(0 e1)\foo([1,2,\ldots])=1+foo([2,2,\ldots])\quad(1 e2)\foo([2,2,2,0,\ldots])=foo([2,2,0,\ldots])\quad(2=2)\foo([2,2,0,\ldots])=foo([2,0,0,\ldots])\quad(2=2)\foo([2,0,0,1,1])=1+foo([0,0,1,1])\quad(2 e0)\foo([0,0,1,1])=foo([0,1,1])\quad(0=0)\foo([0,1,1])=1+foo([1,1])\quad(0 e1)\foo([1,1])=foo([1])\quad(1=1)\foo([1])=1\quad( ext{base case, size}=1)\end{array}[/latex]

Unwinding: [latex]foo([1,1])=1[/latex], [latex]foo([0,1,1])=1+1=2[/latex], [latex]foo([0,0,1,1])=2[/latex], [latex]foo([2,0,0,1,1])=1+2=3[/latex], [latex]foo([2,2,0,\ldots])=3[/latex], [latex]foo([2,2,2,\ldots])=3[/latex], [latex]foo([1,2,\ldots])=1+3=4[/latex], [latex]foo([0,1,\ldots])=1+4=5[/latex].

Answer: 5
